summary: Alfred Foucher worked in Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1885 and later held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1901–1914) and the University of Paris (~1914–1937).
Alfred Gell studied at the London School of Economics and Political Science from around 1968 to 1972. He later held an academic post at the same institution from circa 1979 until 1997.

Indologist Alfred Hillebrandt studied at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler (~1872–1875) and at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1875–1877). He served as a professor at the University of Breslau from circa 1887 to 1924.

Alfred Ludwig worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Vienna, Berlin under Albrecht Weber, Moriz Haupt, Friedrich Müller, and Anton Boller. After habilitating at Vienna in 1858, he held professorships at Charles University from 1860, becoming full professor in 1871.

Alicia Turner specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Chicago, where she studied under doctoral supervisors Bruce Lincoln and Steven Collins, along with Saw Tun, Daw Than Than Win, John Okell, and Carol S. Anderson.

Alison Denton Jones works in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Martin King Whyte, committee member Christopher Winship, and teachers Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret Dornish.

Allan G. Grapard worked in Japanology and religious studies. From around 1985 to 2010, he held posts at the University of California and UC Santa Barbara, serving as ISF Professor of Shinto Studies and teaching in the Department of Religious Studies.

Philosopher Allan Gibbard studied at Swarthmore College (~1960–1964) and Harvard University (~1965–1971). He held positions at the University of Chicago (~1969–1977), the University of Pittsburgh (~1974–1975), and the University of Michigan (around 1977).
Sinologist Allan H. Barr completed his doctorate at the University of Oxford by 1983. He served as Professor of Asian Languages and Literatures at Pomona College, where his post is attested in 2001.

Indologist Allen Wright Thrasher studied under doctoral supervisor Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1967–1977) and traditional teachers Vighnahari Bhalacandra Deo, R. Srinivasan Raghavachariar, and K. A. Sivaramakrishna Sastri. He worked at the Library of Congress (~1985–2013).
Alnis Dickson specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned an MA at McGill University, attested in 2009, studying under MA supervisor Lara Braitstein and teacher G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Aloys Sprenger, active in Indology, studied at the University of Vienna (~1832–1836). He served as principal of Delhi College (~1845–1848), Aliah University (~1850–1856), and Hooghly Mohsin College (1851–1854), followed by a post at the University of Bern (~1858–1881).

Alvappillai Veluppillai worked in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics, studying at Oxford (~1962–1964). He held posts at Kerala (~1973–1974), Edinburgh (~1979–1980), Virginia (~1980–1981), Arizona State as Professor of Religious Studies (~1990–2000), and Uppsala University (~1990–2005).

Amalananda Ghosh worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at University College London (~1936–1937), he served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India from around 1953 to 1968.

Amanda K. Goodman works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed a PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, supervised by Robert H. Sharf, Luis Oscar Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr., and later took a teaching post at the University of Toronto.

Amar Singh specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under doctoral supervisor Anthony Kennedy Warder and teachers Bimal Krishna Matilal, T. Venkatacharya, Alasdair Urquhart, and Rahul Sankrityayan (1960–1963).

Amaranatha Jha studied at Colonelganj Inter College and Muir Central College (~1913–1917), where he became Professor of English in 1917. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Allahabad (~1938–1947) and Banaras Hindu University (~1947–1948), and Vice-President of Ganganatha Jha Research Institute (~1943–1955).

Philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar Amber D. Carpenter studied under M. M. McCabe, Verity Harte, Raimond Gaita, Jonathan Lear, Susan Neiman, and Jonathan Glover. Her posts include Yale-NUS College, University of St Andrews, Einstein Forum (2008), York, and Melbourne.
Amelia Hall works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies and completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford by 2012. In 2019, she held posts at Naropa University and Central Michigan University.
Amita Chatterjee is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who served as a professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University, attested in 1999 and 2009.
